name: Anthropic context-engineering guidance (trim CLAUDE.md, replace NEVER rules with judgment, skills on demand)
evidence: Could not fetch claude.com/blog directly (DNS blocked in this sandbox); the July 24 2026 post is corroborated by multiple secondary writeups (aiweekly, techstrong, i-scoop, dotzlaw) that quote 'We removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt' and name author Thariq Shihipar. The official docs now encode the same guidance: code.claude.com/docs/en/memory says target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, remove conflicting instructions, run /doctor prompt-audit; /doctor trims 'content Claude can derive from the codebase' and keeps 'pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults'. code.claude.com/docs/en/costs: 'Aim to keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines'.
what_it_does: Anthropic's own guidance for Claude 5-era models: thin CLAUDE.md (purpose + gotchas), move procedures into skills that load on demand, delete stacked NEVER/ALWAYS rules that conflict.
claimed_in_videos: Anthropic cut 80%+ of the system prompt with 0% eval loss; keep CLAUDE.md to repo purpose + gotchas; run /doctor to right-size.
reality_check: Holds. The 80% figure and 'no measurable loss' are Anthropic's own internal evals (not independent), but the operational advice is now literally in the official docs and tooling.
why: Haji runs many repos with Claude Code; a bloated or self-contradicting CLAUDE.md silently degrades every session and costs tokens on every turn. This is the single highest-leverage, zero-cost change in the whole theme.
how_to_adopt: In each repo: run `/doctor` then `/doctor prompt-audit` (needs Claude Code v2.1.283+). Accept the trims, move procedure-like sections into .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .claude/rules/ with paths: frontmatter. Target under 200 lines.
risks: Trim one repo first and watch behaviour for a week; some NEVER rules exist because of a real past incident and should become a PreToolUse hook rather than be deleted.

name: Claude Code /doctor (and /doctor prompt-audit)
evidence: Commands reference (fetched 2026-10-10): '/doctor [prompt-audit [path]]' is a bundled skill; checkup covers installation health, unused skills/MCP/plugins vs context cost, CLAUDE.md duplication and derivable content, permissions; prompt-audit requires v2.1.283+; alias /checkup. `claude doctor` in the terminal is read-only diagnostics.
what_it_does: Setup checkup that proposes CLAUDE.md trims and migrations into skills, flags unused extensions, and (prompt-audit) finds outdated or conflicting instructions.

name: Claude Code /code-review ultra (alias /ultrareview)
evidence: Official doc fetched 2026-10-10: research preview; runs a fleet of reviewer agents in an Anthropic cloud sandbox; findings independently reproduced; needs claude.ai login; Pro and Max get 3 free runs (one-time, no refresh), then $5-$25 per review billed to usage credits; 5-10 min per run; diff limit 500 files / 8,000 lines; `claude ultrareview` subcommand for CI; not on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or ZDR orgs.
what_it_does: Deep multi-agent cloud code review of a branch or PR with verified findings.
claimed_in_videos: Spins up a fleet of cloud agents to hunt bugs; Pro/Max get three free until May 5th.
reality_check: Real. The 'until May 5th' deadline was 2026 and has passed; the 3 free runs still exist per the current doc and are one-time. After that it is $5-25 per run in usage credits, which must be enabled.

evidence: Official doc: bundled skill; runs as a background forked subagent (v2.1.218+); effort levels low..max; --fix applies findings, --comment posts to GitHub PR/GitLab MR; counts against normal plan usage; reports correctness bugs (plus cleanups at higher effort).

name: Claude Code /effort
evidence: Commands reference: `/effort [level|auto|status|ultracode [on|off]]`, levels low to xhigh, max (session-only), auto; `status` prints the current level; the `ultracode` setting persists via settings key; changing mid-turn triggers a prompt-cache warning.

claimed_in_videos: An interactive slider from low to 'ultra'.
reality_check: Mostly right; it is a level argument (and a picker in /model), not a literal slider; 'max' is session-only, other levels can be set as defaults.

risks: Changing effort mid-session can invalidate the prompt cache (docs warn); change it at natural breakpoints.

name: Claude Code /loop (scheduled tasks)
evidence: Official doc: `/loop [interval] [prompt]`, e.g. `/loop 5m check the deploy`; 1-minute minimum; session must stay open (or be backgrounded); self-pacing mode when interval omitted; built-in maintenance prompt or .claude/loop.md; tasks expire after 7 days; jitter delays runs; can chain skills like `/loop 20m /code-review`.
cost: free (plan usage; each fire resends full context)
what_it_does: Re-run a prompt or skill on an interval inside a session, or let Claude self-pace.
claimed_in_videos: 'Check the deploy every 5 minutes and then done'.
reality_check: Exactly as claimed, plus more (loop.md, self-pacing, one-shot reminders). Cost caveat: each iteration resends the full conversation context.
why: Replaces Haji babysitting CI/deploys. Pair with a short context (run /clear first) to keep each fire cheap.
how_to_adopt: `/loop 10m check CI on this PR and fix failures` from a fresh session; for anything unattended use Routines (cloud, 1h min) or Desktop scheduled tasks instead.
risks: Fires only while the session is open and idle; loops in a long bloated session burn plan usage fast (docs explicitly flag this).

name: Claude Code /mcp
evidence: Commands reference: `/mcp [reconnect|enable|disable [<server>|all]]` manages server connections and OAuth. MCP *prompts* exposed by a server appear as commands of the form `/mcp__<server>__<prompt>`; tool definitions are deferred until used.
what_it_does: Manage MCP server connections and OAuth from inside a session.
claimed_in_videos: After connecting Slack/Notion etc., each shows up as its own slash command (/slack, /notion, /calendar).
reality_check: Partly wrong. /mcp manages connections; servers do not become `/slack`-style commands. Only MCP prompts become `/mcp__server__prompt` commands. Connected tools are used by Claude when relevant.
why: Useful mainly for `/mcp disable` on servers you are not using in a session, which cuts context (docs: prefer CLIs like gh/gcloud over MCP for context efficiency).
how_to_adopt: Run `/mcp` and disable idle servers; run `/context` to see what MCP costs you.
risks: None beyond the mis-description in the video.

name: caveman (JuliusBrussee/caveman)
evidence: GitHub API: 110,876 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-10, created 2026-04-04. README: skill (/caveman, /ultracave, /megacave) + optional local proxy that compresses inputs (logs/CSV/JSON) 33.2% fewer input tokens; skill benchmark on 10 dev questions with Opus 5.5: 6,983 output tokens (no instruction) vs 4,334 ('Answer concisely') vs 4,119 (/caveman) vs 2,693 (/ultracave); third-party: JetBrains 8.5% fewer output tokens on 86 tasks with no quality loss, Elastic 63.6% fewer response tokens; skill text costs ~1,160 tokens of context. Install `/plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman` then `/plugin install caveman@caveman`.
what_it_does: Makes Claude answer in terse 'caveman' prose; optional proxy shrinks tool outputs before they hit context.
claimed_in_videos: Claimed 65% token cut; creator measured ~30% fewer output tokens on two tasks with same quality.
reality_check: The TikTok fact-check is directionally right. The author's own numbers show /caveman is only ~5% better than simply saying 'Answer concisely'; the big wins are /ultracave and the input-side proxy. Output tokens are a minority of a typical Claude Code session (cache reads dominate), so a 30% output cut moves total spend by far less.
why: Cheap A/B for Haji's usage limits, but the honest expectation is single-digit to ~20% total savings on real coding sessions. The proxy (input compression of logs/test output) is the more interesting half for a builder who runs tests constantly.
how_to_adopt: Install the plugin, run the same three real tasks with and without, compare `/usage`. Or skip the plugin and put one line in CLAUDE.md: 'Answer tersely; code, paths and commands verbatim.'
risks: Terse mode can drop nuance in security warnings and multi-step explanations (README carves these out); proxy is a local MITM of tool output.

evidence: GitHub API: 160,184 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-10-10, created 2026-06-12. README (fetched): author-run benchmark with Opus 5.5, 39 tasks x 5 runs: Ponytail 5 = 47% of baseline LOC, 55% output tokens, 74% cost, 59% time; commands /ponytail-review, /ponytail-audit, /ponytail-debt; install `/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail` then `/plugin install ponytail@ponytail`. Independent: JetBrains AI blog (July 2026) ran 80 paired tasks and measured -15% code, -10.3% cost, -11% time, no quality difference, concluding savings are 'a quarter to a half of what is advertised'.
what_it_does: A YAGNI/'laziest senior dev' skill that makes Claude write less code and refactor toward reuse; adds review/audit/debt commands.
claimed_in_videos: Cuts Claude usage by 50%+ with no quality loss (Nate Herk); -39% tokens / -27% cost (Duncan Rogoff's README table); 'gigantic de-bloating tool' (youraveragetechbro).
reality_check: Real, hugely popular, maintained. The 50% claims are the author's own benchmark; the only independent test found ~10% cost savings and ~15% less code. Savings depend on how much over-building the task invites; greenfield work sees less.
why: Less code is a maintainability win for a solo founder even if the cost saving is ~10%. Try it mainly for /ponytail-review on PRs, and compare against the built-in /simplify before keeping both.
how_to_adopt: Install via marketplace; run `/ponytail-audit` once on an existing app and `/ponytail-review` on the next PR; keep it only if the diffs are visibly leaner than /simplify's.
risks: Overlaps with /simplify and pstack's unslop; stacking all three bloats context and can produce contradictory style edits.

name: Per-feature verification skills (pattern: a skills folder that teaches the agent how to test each part of the app)
evidence: Pattern is implementable natively: Claude Code bundled `/verify` skill ('build your project's app, run it, and observe the result'), microsoft/playwright-mcp (37,994 stars) for browser driving, and skills with supporting files. Cursor cloud agent / Devin 'recorded browser session' has no exact Claude Code equivalent; Playwright MCP screenshots attached to the PR are the substitute.
what_it_does: For each app area keep a SKILL.md describing how to navigate, what to click and the expected result; Claude runs it (browser MCP) after each change and attaches screenshots; a pre-PR step keeps the skills current.
claimed_in_videos: Creator merges PRs without reading code by reviewing agent-run verification recordings; ships ~30 PRs/day.
reality_check: The pattern is sound and the tooling exists in Claude Code today. 'Merge without reading code' is the creator's risk appetite, not evidence; the real metric (post-merge defect rate) is not shown.

how_to_adopt: Add `.claude/skills/verify-<feature>/SKILL.md` for the 3 riskiest flows in one app (signup, payment, core action); install Playwright MCP (`claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest`); require `/verify` plus screenshots before any PR; add a 'maintain verification skills' step to the ship checklist.
risks: Screenshots are not assertions; keep real tests for money and auth paths. Browser runs cost tokens; scope them.

what_it_does: Captures what Claude does in each session, compresses it, and injects relevant memories into future sessions.

name: Jev classifier (TypeSafe AI) via jev-mcp-server
evidence: typesafe.ai unreachable from sandbox. Secondary sources (aiweekly, litellm docs pass-through page, cloudprice, llmreference, Sept 2026 guides): Jev is TypeSafe AI's non-generative classifier/scoring model, model id jev-latest, endpoint api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, $0.042 per 1M input tokens with free output, no free tier/trial, early access via waitlist, company reportedly raised $40M. Several community MCP servers exist (burnigtm/jev-mcp 62 stars, blakestone-x/jev-mcp 25, wangkuangkuang/jev-mcp-server 3); the `uvx jev-mcp-server install claude-code` command on screen matches an official-looking quickstart.
what_it_does: Fast, cheap yes/no and scoring classifier used here to tag exported chat history as got_it_right/got_it_wrong.
claimed_in_videos: Tag every conversation for mistakes and style, then reverse-engineer custom instructions; 'there was never a Jarvis'.
reality_check: Jev exists and is cheap; it is not needed for this job (Haiku can tag 1,000 chats for a few dollars) and sending your whole chat history to a third-party classifier is the main cost, not money.
why: The pattern (mine corrections into a <1,500-char instruction block) is good; the vendor is unnecessary. Do it with Claude Code + Haiku on the local export.
how_to_adopt: Export Claude data (Settings > Privacy > Export) and ChatGPT data; run a Claude Code script with `model: haiku` subagents over conversations.json extracting corrections; generate the instruction block; put it in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.
risks: Privacy of full chat history; Jev early-access terms unknown; Claude export does not include Claude Code sessions (those live in ~/.claude/projects).

name: Context Transfer prompt (/contexttransfer handoff block)
evidence: Full prompt is on screen in the video. The '39% dumber' figure traces to Laban et al., 'LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation' (arXiv 2505.06120; ICLR 2026 oral): average 39% drop across six tasks in multi-turn vs single-turn (v1 caption said 35%); cause is early assumptions and premature answers. claude.ai supports custom skills; Claude Code has /compact and native handoff via CLAUDE.md surviving compaction.

why: Haji already runs session-handoff; this five-section structure is a good checklist for it and for claude.ai threads. Zero cost.
how_to_adopt: Save the on-screen prompt as a claude.ai skill named 'Context Transfer'; in Claude Code keep using the session-handoff skill and `/compact <focus>`.
risks: None.
